messages:
alex: Hey team — escalated from support. Customer t-acme seeing recurring 504s and long tail latency on hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. They report p99 token latency hitting 20s and a bunch of 502/504s. Can we triage? :warning:

support-bot: Incident created: INC-1769994322. Pager notified. Link: https://internal.redwood/incident/1769994322 :rotating_light:

maria: cc @sam @devon — any immediate telemetry? Which queue is blowing up?

sam: digging into ingress metrics now. early look: request_queue_depth for hosted-gateway spiked from avg 12 -> 320 at 09:11 UTC. Continuous-batcher backlog increased in same window. Looks like KV cache miss rate also rose.

alex: Customer provided sample request id: r-0a9c3e2f and curl repro. They say it happens intermittently but more under burst load.

alex: curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this..."}]}'
```

devon: logs from the gateway around r-0a9c3e2f:
```
[09:10:58] INFO  incoming request r-0a9c3e2f tenant=t-acme
[09:11:03] WARN  request_queue_dequeue_timeout tenant=t-acme elapsed=3000ms
[09:11:03] ERROR handler: request failed status=504 reason="queue tail timeout"
```

sam: looks like our dequeue deadline (3s) expired repeatedly leading to early 504s; but the p99 token latency higher suggests once dequeued some requests still live long due to continuous-batcher backlog. Kernel: continuous-batcher backlog=480 items, avg batch size=24, batch build time spiking.

maria: Any recent deploys or config changes to batching thresholds or queue caps?

sam: No infra deploys at that timestamp. I see one autoscaler decision at 09:09 to not scale because CPU utilization < threshold. This smells like queue saturation from many small requests that defeat batching heuristics and flood request queue depth.

alex: Customer says they ramped traffic (traffic generator for load test) — they think they hit a threshold. They're asking for mitigation while we investigate.

devon: Quick mitigations we can try: 1) increase max_queue_depth for hosted-gateway for that AZ/cluster; 2) temporarily lower continuous-batcher max_wait_ms to favor smaller batches (reduces batch build time); 3) route tenant to a spare pool with higher capacity. Which is lowest-risk?

maria: 3) requires tenant routing change and possible warmup. 1) config bump is fastest but risky if it just increases memory pressure. 2) safer and likely helps tail latency at cost of throughput.

sam: I can flip batch max_wait_ms from 250ms -> 100ms for the affected pool and watch. Rolling change with a small canary. Will do now. :eyes:

support-bot: Change request logged: CFG-176999-1 by sam — batch.max_wait_ms=100ms for pool hosted-eu-1 (canary first).

sam: Canary applied to 2 hosts at 09:22 UTC. Monitoring: request_queue_depth dropping from 320 -> 78 within 90s. p95 token latency falling from 6s -> 1.8s.

alex: Customer confirmed improvement briefly but still saw a few 504s at 09:25. They provided another request id r-0b7d4f1c.

devon: Check KV cache behavior for those requests. If batching reduces, KV cache miss amplification can increase per-request compute.

sam: KV cache miss rate for tenant t-acme jumped from 8% -> 42% during ramp. Most long requests correspond to cold KV cache misses and some model variant fallbacks that elongated inference.

maria: Action items so far:
- sam: keep batch.max_wait_ms=100ms for 10m and monitor (in progress)
- devon: prepare a short-lived tenant routing to spare pool if degradation persists
- alex: ask customer to throttle ramp or use a throttled test harness while we stabilize

alex: customer's immediate ask: ETA to fully mitigate? They have paying customers seeing errors.

sam: If current change holds, expect >90% reduction in 504s in 10 mins. If not, we'll move to routing step which is ~8-12min to shift and warm.

devon: Long-term: we should add adaptive batching thresholds that detect KV cache missstorms and temporarily favor lower max_wait_ms per-tenant. I'll log RFC.

maria: Sam — can you paste quick graphs and the spike window for the incident channel?

sam: Graph links: 
- queue depth: https://internal.redwood/metrics?graph=queue_depth&window=15m&anchor=1769994322
- kv miss rate: https://internal.redwood/metrics?graph=kv_miss&tenant=t-acme

alex: Customer updated: after your change 09:24->09:35 errors dropped to single digits, they paused load test. Thank you. :thumbsup:

support-bot: INC-1769994322 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Will auto-close if stable for 1 hour.

maria: Postmortem checklist: capture exact sequence (traffic ramp -> kv miss storm -> batching backlog -> dequeue timeouts), owner for routing playbook, and ticket to add per-tenant adaptive batching heuristics.

alex: I'll keep the customer updated and open a support ticket with next steps. Closing thread for now but will re-open if it recurs.
